Use cases

What coding agents use XERJ for, with the measurements

Agents use XERJ to read code they do not know before they write it, to search the folder they are working in without pulling whole files into context, and to audit a codebase by querying facts instead of reading every file. Each use case below links a write-up with the commands and the measured result, including where it did not help.

For coding agents

Read the reference before writing the code

Reference coding · case study

2.7× fewer output tokens than grep, same 16/16 solved

The agent retrieves how the nearest open-source projects solved the task, then writes the code. Over 8 tasks in 4 languages: 9,982 output tokens with XERJ, 26,477 grep-driven, 260,916 from memory (11/16 solved). On 13 purpose-built libraries the model had never seen, 21/21 correct with retrieval against 1/21 from memory.

Read the case study → Ask a library · no clone

One question, one signed pack, file:line back

xerj "how does lz4 frame format work" answered from a 4.4 MB pack in 1.75 s on first use, then a definition lookup in 0.022 s. Each hit names the pin and the licence; approach-only sources say "read, do not copy".

xerj ask →

For security review

Audit a codebase by querying it

Method

Index as security facts, read only the violators

One document per function with its taint sources, sinks and call edges. Compile the rule into a query; read only what it returns.

The method → Case study · WordPress core

1,492 files for about 26,000 tokens

Roughly 619,000 lines, audited for about 26,000 tokens against about 5,200,000 to load the tree once, with per-phase costs. Three Medium-severity results, none claimed as a 0-day.

Read it → Case study · XERJ's own Rust

A real DoS for 10,533 tokens

XERJ indexed its own engine and found an unauthenticated stack-overflow denial of service for 10,533 tokens instead of 1.8 million. The fix shipped.

Read it →

For your own files

Search a folder, remember what you learned

Zero-token search

Code, PDFs and notes in one local index

xerj autoindex <folder>, then ask in plain words. No model runs to search, so finding the file spends no tokens and nothing leaves the machine.

Three real runs → Second brain

Every link shows the text that made it

xerj brain ~/notes turns a folder into a timestamped link index; 121 files gave 364 links. It makes your structure queryable; it does not understand your notes.

Second brain → Agent memory

Store, recall, forget per namespace

POST /_memory/<ns> and /_recall, or the two MCP memory tools. Each namespace is its own index.

Memory recipe →

For search and analytics

Retrieval and aggregation on one node

RAG retrieval

BM25, kNN and hybrid in one query

One planner for text and vectors. kNN at k=10 measured a tie with Elasticsearch 8.13.4 (1.76 ms against 2.08 ms p50, 100% recall on both).

AI search → Semantic analytics

Aggregate over the retrieved neighbours

One POST /_search runs aggregations over the top-k set, so a question gets exact buckets and grounded examples together. A correctness demo, not a benchmark.

Semantic analytics → Postgres CDC

One hybrid query instead of two

Logical-replication CDC keeps XERJ in sync with Postgres; one RRF query replaces the tsvector plus pgvector merge in the app.

Read it →

Classic Elasticsearch workloads (SIEM, log analytics, observability, full-text, vector RAG) are written up as playbooks, and moving an existing cluster is in Migrate from Elasticsearch. Against Elasticsearch 8.13.4 the closed-loop benchmark scored 55 wins, 26 ties and 4 losses, all four losses read p99 under a write flood (benchmarks).

Before you pick a use case

Where it does not pay

  • Popular libraries. On code the model has memorised, retrieval is neutral to harmful and only adds cost.
  • Meaning-based search out of the box. The default embedder is lexical. Use --embed-mode neural when matching by meaning matters.
  • Clusters. XERJ is a single node with no replication. Use Elasticsearch or OpenSearch where you need one.

Try the first one in 30 seconds

curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | sh && ~/.local/bin/xerj "how does lz4 frame format work"
